source.title: FISHER: A Foundation Model for Multimodal Industrial Signal Comprehensive Representation
source.authors: Ping-Yi Fan; An-Bai Jiang; Shu-Wei Zhang; Zhiqiang Lv; Bing Han; Xin-Hu Zheng; Wen-Rui Liang; Junjie Li; Wei-Qiang Zhang; Yanmin Qian; Xie Chen; Cheng Lu; Jia Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates downstream benchmark performance across sizes of an industrial-signal representation model, a different modality and task setting from language-model scaling.
record.gate_note: The paper does not measure held-out cross-entropy, fit loss power laws, or test compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. The relevant results are industrial-signal downstream scores across FISHER sizes; they are not evidence about language-model loss scaling.
record.test_reason: FISHER is an industrial-signal encoder, not a language model. It measures no pretraining loss, fits no power law and makes no prediction. Its loose 'efficient scaling curve' remark rests on downstream KNN scores for three sizes (5.5M–22M), with no fit or loss link. So it bears on no version: V1–V4 and V6 concern language models, and V5 needs a power-law form.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that FISHER beats 24 baselines on RMIS at much smaller sizes. They attribute its gains to adapting to native high sampling rates, and find audio plus music pretraining data better than industrial signals. The 'efficient scaling curve' is a score-versus-size comparison against baselines (Fig. 1), not a fitted scaling law.
record.recipe_differences: No language-model loss-scaling recipe is tested; this is an industrial-signal representation model evaluated on downstream KNN benchmarks.
record.method_sensitivity: FISHER size (tiny, mini, small); few-shot shot count.

fits_no_version.finding: Across three FISHER sizes (5.5M, 10M, 22M), downstream scores rise slightly. SRMIS goes 61.12→61.43→62.23, and few-shot mean accuracy goes 33.20→33.52→34.30. No scaling fit is made.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream performance of self-supervised industrial-signal encoders improves monotonically but modestly with parameter count over a narrow size range.

record.problems: Only three FISHER sizes are compared, over a parameter range of 5.5M to 22M; no scaling-law fit, predictive extrapolation, or uncertainty estimates are reported for these scores.
record.rows_left_out: Table II reports separate scores for the individual RMIS sub-datasets for FISHER sizes; those per-dataset results were omitted to keep the record focused on the aggregate scaling measures. The paper also reports a few-shot mean and each shot-count result, all included above.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss and no power law in parameters, data or compute.
No fixed-parameter shape comparison. The variants differ in width, heads and bandwidth together.
Non-text modality, but no power-law fit of loss or performance.
No language models. Downstream scores for three encoder sizes, with no predictive fit and no link to pretraining loss.
No exponents or fitting choices compared.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'tests/T3' and V6 'supports' label are rejected: the model is not a language model and no scaling law is fitted or tested. The size comparison spans only 4x in parameters, the variants also change other hyperparameters (d, heads, bandwidth, batch size), and no uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or power-law relationship in parameters, tokens, or compute is measured.
No power-law fits or small-run predictions of larger-run loss are reported.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or parameter/token growth trend is tested.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count is reported.
The study uses audio and music data to pretrain industrial-signal encoders, but does not test whether a power-law loss form holds in another modality or training regime.

Tests downstream benchmark scores across three FISHER sizes in industrial signal analysis, not language models; does not relate scores to pretraining loss, fit a predictive scaling law, or test other model families.
No comparison of loss-law exponents or allocation trends across fitting choices or setups is made.

rows.subject: FISHER-tiny
rows.stage_stated: Pre-trained on audio and music data; evaluated without fine-tuning
rows.operation_detail: Compared downstream RMIS scores across FISHER model sizes
rows.note: Aggregate across the anomaly-detection datasets.
rows.check: All rows are downstream KNN scores of a non-language industrial-signal encoder at three sizes. They are not language-model results (V6) and carry no power-law fit (V5). Values match Tables II and IV. Gains are small: SFD goes 63.13→63.25→63.31 and SRMIS 61.12→61.43→62.23.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: FISHER sizes from 5.5M to 22M on aggregate RMIS and few-shot fault-diagnosis scores
reader_labels.reason: Aggregate SAD, SFD, SRMIS, few-shot scores at each shot count, and the reported few-shot means rise across the three sizes (r1–r27). This supports a size-performance trend in this tested setting, not a language-model scaling law.
